pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: src/app/api/agents/forge-ability/route.ts:96 The forge-ability route forwards a prompt string the client built straight to Gemini, so the server has no assembler, budget, trust classification or fingerprint for it; the sibling one-shot/step route refuses to accept client prompt strings for this very reason.

techniques.evidence: src/app/api/agents/forge-ability/route.ts:96 A pre-rendered prompt arrives from the call site instead of typed inputs. The one-shot/step route (line 261, buildStepProducePrompt) is the conformant counter-example in the same context.

src/app/api/agents/forge-ability/route.ts:48 A fixed ceiling explained by a comment but never derived from a measured length distribution. Truncation is detected (line 110) but there is no escalate-on-cut retry.
src/app/api/one-shot/step/route.ts:46 Client evidence comes in as typed input with an enumerated kind, and malformed entries are dropped instead of rendering as empty holes.

pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: src/hooks/useModuleCLI.ts:46 buildTaskPrompt calls itself the single code path, but the hook also exports a raw-string sendPrompt door; about 29 call sites across the repo pass pre-rendered prompt text through it, outside the assembler's budget, variant resolution and review.

techniques.evidence: src/hooks/useModuleCLI.ts:46 The assembler output is a plain string and the dispatch door is unsealed, so call sites send their own rendered prompts.
src/lib/cli-task.ts:691 The assembler has no global budget, floors or degradation ladder; searching cli-task.ts, cli-task-handlers.ts and prompt-context.ts for budget/truncat/MAX_ found nothing.
src/lib/cli-task.ts:751 Prior model output (a review's nextSteps) becomes the task prompt with no declared trust class; CLITask.prompt is an untyped raw string.
src/lib/cli-task.ts:84 The callback section gives a machine-checkable done shape (a JSON schema between exact markers) that the terminal validates.
